build_status_cat_url.description: Turn an HTTP status code into the address of its cat, ready to drop into a Slack alert, an email, an incident note or a README, with ready-made HTML and Markdown snippets beside it. Nothing is downloaded, so this is the cheap way to put a cat on a failed request. A code the site has no cat for fails the step and names the nearest codes it has, unless the class's cat is allowed instead, in which case 520 gets the 500 cat and the result says so.
build_status_cat_url.display_str_template: Build the HTTP Cats URL for status {0}.
build_status_cat_url.name: build_status_cat_url

parameters.description: The HTTP status code to get the cat for. Pick one from the list, or wire in the status an earlier step got back: a number such as 404, or text such as '404' or '404 Not Found', all work.
parameters.name: status_code

parameters.description: Optional, off by default. HTTP Cats has a cat for 78 codes, not every one a server can send. Off, a code it has no cat for fails the step and names the nearest codes it does have. On, the cat for the code's class is used instead (500 Internal Server Error for any 5xx, 400 Bad Request for any 4xx) and the result says so, which is the setting to use when the code comes from a live HTTP response.
parameters.name: fallback_to_class

check_service_status.description: Check whether HTTP Cats is up and serving pictures, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being reachable but answering with something other than a picture is reported separately from being down.

description: Put a cat on every HTTP status code with HTTP Cats, the free keyless picture site at http.cat: a cat that is 404 Not Found, a cat that is 418 I'm a teapot, one for each of 78 codes. Build the link for a code to drop into a Slack alert, an email or a README, download the picture as a file to attach, get it inline as a data URI, look a code up to learn its name and class, search the codes by a word in the name, or pick one at random for a cat of the day. Feed it the status an HTTP step got back and a failed request comes with its own cat.
